def total_for_name_refill(names, values):
    """The Copper Kettle is the kind of cafe where the till tape tells
    the whole story of a day. Every sale gets punched in with a short
    name and an amount, and by closing time the tape is a long scroll
    of espresso shots, day-old scones, oat-milk upcharges, and the
    occasional comped drink logged with a minus sign. Marisol, who owns
    the place, has transcribed today's tape into two parallel lists for
    you: names is a list of strings and values is a list of ints of the
    same length; names[i] and values[i] describe the same item. What
    she actually wants to know tonight is how the refill program is
    doing. Regulars who bring their own cups back get rung up under a
    single label, and Marisol would like one number for the day rather
    than a scavenger hunt down the tape. Return the sum of the values
    of the items whose name is exactly the string 'refill' (0 if there
    are none). Some days the regulars stay home and the tape carries no
    such entries at all; Marisol still wants her number, even if it's a
    quiet one. Write the function so she can run it on any day's tape,
    rain or shine, long scroll or short.

    >>> total_for_name_refill([], [])
    0
    >>> total_for_name_refill(['dyn', 'refill', 'eel', 'ax', 'bolt', 'eel', 'refill'], [-1, 5, 4, -1, 28, 20, 29])
    34
    """
